                    ### Question
                    A 19-year-old college student presents to student health with 1 day of fever and chills. He says that he has also been coughing for 2 days. His roommate was sick 3 days ago with similar symptoms and was diagnosed with Mycoplasma infection. He has otherwise been healthy and has had all the required vaccines as scheduled. He is currently taking introductory biology as part of his premedical studies and recently learned about antibodies. He therefore asks his physician about what his body is doing to fight off the infection. At this stage of his infection, which of the following forms are the antibodies circulating in his serum?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The 19-year-old student presents with symptoms consistent with a respiratory infection, likely due to Mycoplasma, as indicated by his roommate's recent illness. In response to this infection, the immune system activates B cells, which begin producing antibodies. The first type of antibody produced in response to an infection is typically Immunoglobulin M (IgM). IgM is known to form a pentameric structure, meaning it consists of five monomer units linked together. This aligns with the consensus that during the early stages of an infection, IgM is the predominant antibody form circulating in the serum. Therefore, the correct answer is that the antibodies circulating in his serum at this stage are primarily pentamers (IgM).
